title: Competitive Programming in C++
under: Self-driven
summary: A living algorithmic library and contest practice archive around advanced data structures, graph algorithms, string algorithms, number theory and ICPC-style problem solving.
points: Achieved 2000+ peak Codeforces rating as Candidate Master and solved 1000+ problems across competitive programming platforms.
Developed expertise in segment trees and variants, centroid decomposition, HLD, Euler tour, binary lifting, suffix trees, FFT/NTT, SCCs and advanced number theory.
Qualified for ICPC World Finals 2026 and repeatedly secured IIT Bombay-best ranks across regional contests.

title: Intelligent Plagiarism Detection System
under: Prof. Ashutosh Gupta · Data Structures and Algorithms
summary: Large-scale code similarity engine combining suffix trees, local alignment, approximate matching and multithreaded C++ pipelines.
points: Implemented Suffix Tree and Ukkonen’s algorithm for efficient linear-time pattern matching across large codebases.
Combined Smith-Waterman local alignment with Levenshtein distance to detect approximate 80% code similarity with fewer false positives.
Supercharged large-scale plagiarism detection using multithreaded C++ parallel processing over code submissions.

title: C Compiler in C++ from Scratch
under: Prof. Uday Khedkar · Implementation of Programming Languages
summary: A structured SCLP compiler for a small C-like language, implemented across parsing, AST construction, semantic analysis and backend lowering.
points: Built SCLP across 5 assignments with parsing, AST construction, semantic analysis, TAC/RTL generation and modular compiler passes.
Engineered a modern C++ codebase using layered class design, inheritance, visitors, virtual dispatch and smart pointers.
Used variant/optional, variadic templates and std::forward to keep the codebase expressive, maintainable and clean.

title: Reinforcement Learning: Bandits, MDP and Game Agents
under: Prof. Shivaram Kalyanakrishnan · Foundations of Intelligent and Learning Agents
summary: A combined RL project suite covering stochastic bandits, MDP planning and adversarial game-playing agents.
points: Implemented UCB, KL-UCB, Thompson Sampling, optimized KL-UCB and Poisson-door policies for stochastic bandits.
Built MDP solvers using Howard’s Policy Iteration and LP, then encoded a strategic card game into an optimal planning pipeline.
Developed Microchess agents with minimax, move ordering and evaluation heuristics against random and rational bots.

title: Medical Image Computing Algorithms
under: Prof. Suyash Awate · Medical Image Computing
summary: Classical and probabilistic medical image algorithms for denoising, CT reconstruction, MRI segmentation, shape modelling and lesion inpainting.
points: Implemented Bayesian MAP-MRF denoising and dictionary-learning patch denoisers for MRI, CT and microscopy images.
Built CT reconstruction using Radon transform, FBP filters and ART for noisy or incomplete projection data.
Segmented brain MRI with bias-corrected FCM and HMRF-GMM-EM using ICM-based label smoothing.
Modelled medical shapes using Procrustes PCA/kernel PCA and benchmarked BrainWeb lesion inpainting methods.

title: Knowledge Representations and Compilation
under: Prof. S. Akshay
summary: Research exploration around tractable Boolean representation languages, synthesis-friendly normal forms and approximate model counting beyond d-DNNF.
points: Explored extensions of Darwiche’s Knowledge Compilation Map through new tractable languages, their relationships and expressiveness.
Investigated synNNF and wDNNF representations for efficient Boolean function synthesis.
Studied model counting beyond d-DNNF using dynamic programming, tree-width heuristics, hashing and d-sharp-based experimentation.

title: Classical and Deep Learning Approaches in NLP
under: Math and Physics Club, IIT Bombay
summary: A broad NLP exploration from traditional text representation to transformers and downstream fine-tuning tasks.
points: Explored NLP pipelines and text representation models such as n-grams, TF-IDF and Word2Vec.
Studied RNNs, LSTMs and Transformer models with attention mechanisms and encoder-decoder frameworks.
Analyzed BERT, contextual embeddings, fine-tuning and applications in sequence classification, pairwise classification and sequence labeling.

title: Machine Unlearning
under: Prof. Pushpak Bhattacharyya · Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
summary: A practical unlearning suite for deep and linear models, with CIFAR-10 experiments and efficient leave-one-out retraining machinery.
points: Implemented fine-tuning, gradient ascent and EIF on CIFAR-10 using PyTorch and ResNet18, combining distillation, entropy maximization and validation-aware fine-tuning.
Built a Streamlit demo for visualizing unlearning behavior and model performance.
Implemented a custom DeltaGrad pipeline for logistic regression using LBFGS Hessian approximation and two-loop recursion.

title: ShellForge
under: Prof. Mythili R. Vutukuru · Operating Systems
summary: Operating systems assignments spanning pthread synchronization, xv6 internals and Linux system call programming.
points: Implemented multithreaded programs using Pthreads, locks, semaphores and condition variables.
Modified xv6 to understand process management, memory management, scheduling, synchronization and file systems.
Developed programs using Linux system call APIs for process control, IPC mechanisms and memory allocation.

title: Combinatorial Game Design and Analysis
under: Prof. Urban Larsson · Combinatorial Game Theory
summary: Design and analysis of impartial L-tile combinatorial games using game trees, canonical forms and automated verification.
points: Designed and analyzed an impartial L-Tile combinatorial game, applying game trees and simplification theorems.
Derived canonical forms for complex positions and studied hot/cold games, periodicity and dyadic game values.
Implemented an automated solver using CGSuite with custom rule logic and verified conjectures for small boards.

title: Reinforcement Learning Trader
under: Web & Coding Club, IIT Bombay
summary: A custom stock-trading environment and deep RL baseline suite exploring DQN, DDQN and DDPG agents.
points: Developed a DQN model with CartPole v1 while learning RL algorithms and built a custom OpenAI Gym environment.
Explored quantitative finance models such as Black-Scholes, arbitrage pricing and mean-reversion strategies for trading-agent design.
Trained DQN, DDQN and DDPG algorithms on a custom stock trading environment.
On GSPC_2018, achieved a hypothetical net worth increase of 5.68% from $20,000 to $21,135, outperforming the stock over 70% of the time.

title: Computer Architecture in Verilog and Assembly
under: Prof. Sayandeep Saha and Prof. Bhaskaran Raman · Digital Logic Design and Computer Architecture
summary: Low-level architecture implementations in Verilog and MIPS assembly, from arithmetic circuits to recursive algorithms.
points: Developed Karatsuba’s multiplication algorithm in Verilog with ripple-carry and carry-lookahead adders.
Implemented both combinational and recursive sequential circuit designs.
Implemented recursive Merge Sort and Binary Search on dynamically allocated arrays using the MIPS ISA.

title: Text Compression and Autocomplete
under: Prof. Ashutosh Gupta · Data Structures and Algorithms
summary: Data-structures project implementing compression and dynamic autocomplete with canonical algorithmic building blocks.
points: Implemented DEFLATE using Huffman coding, achieving about 2:1 compression on large text files.
Used Lempel-Ziv’77 (LZ77) for lossless compression through back-referencing.
Developed dynamic context-based autocomplete using Prefix Trie and KMP.

title: DateSphere
under: Prof. Kameswari Chebrolu · Software Systems Lab
summary: A full-stack dating website with profile management, authentication, filters, swiping-style discovery and recommendation logic.
points: Developed a dating website using HTML, CSS and JavaScript with profile updates, password recovery and customizable filters.
Enhanced UI with like counts, profile swiping and a side menu for seamless navigation.
Built server-side Node.js support for authentication, profile management, session handling and a scoring algorithm for recommendations.

title: GeoGuide
under: e-Yantra Robotics Competition
summary: Computer vision and geospatial robotics tasks around event extraction, object classification, path tracking and ArUco markers.
points: Developed advanced image-processing tasks, object classification using ResNet-18, path tracking with ArUco markers and event extraction from arena images.
Designed CSV-based path tracking and validation for ArUco ID latitude-longitude data under simulated live tracking.
Built a coordinate tracking system using QGIS for spatial visualization and optimized ArUco ID tracking.

title: Cryptography
under: Cyber Security Community, IIT Bombay
summary: Classical and modern cryptography study with hands-on cipher implementations and RSA oracle attack experiments.
points: Studied RSA, one-time pad, digital signatures, cryptographic hash functions, block and stream ciphers, AES and Diffie-Hellman key exchange.
Implemented Hill cipher encryption/decryption.
Implemented an adaptive ciphertext attack on RSA using a parity oracle.

title: Group Theory and Theoretical CS
under: Math and Physics Club, IIT Bombay
summary: Mathematical foundations project covering algebra, number theory, first-order logic, proof theory and automata theory.
points: Explored group theory basics such as binary operations, groups, subgroups, cosets and Lagrange’s theorem.
Applied homomorphisms and Burnside’s lemma to symmetry and number-theoretic reasoning.
Studied number theory, first-order logic, proof theory, unification and automata theory including DFA, NFA, regular languages and Turing machines.

title: Corridor Board Game
under: Self-driven
summary: C++ implementation of the Corridor board game with dynamic memory management, movement logic and graph-search validation.
points: Developed the board game Corridor in C++ using object-oriented programming and pointers for dynamic memory management.
Optimized game mechanics and player movement logic.
Implemented BFS and backtracking algorithms to assess existence of valid paths.

title: Quadcopter
under: Prof. Kushal Tuckley · Makerspace
summary: Hardware and control project assembling a WiFi-controlled quadcopter with sensors and PID-based stabilization.
points: Studied quadcopter dynamics and control theory, implementing a PID controller for stabilization.
Assembled a quadcopter from scratch using ESP32, Arduino and sensors such as barometer, IMU and GPS.
Enabled mobile-app control through WiFi joystick input.

title: Sudoku Solver with Image Processing
under: Self-driven
summary: Image-based Sudoku extraction and solving pipeline combining OCR, OpenCV, deep learning and backtracking.
points: Developed an image-based Sudoku solver using OCR for digit recognition and planned web hosting.
Implemented an OpenCV pipeline to extract, digitize and solve Sudoku puzzles from images.
Combined deep learning-based recognition with classical backtracking for final puzzle solving.
